item.title: Finite Subgroups of Birational Automorphism Groups of Severi--Brauer Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.09981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a finite group acting birationally on a non-trivial Severi--Brauer surface $S$ over a field $\mathbb{K}$ of positive characteristic not equal to $3$ is isomorphic either to a subgroup of group of biregular automorphisms of $S_{\mathbb{K}^{per}}$ or to a subgroup of $\mu^3_3$, where $\mu_3$ is a cyclic group of order $3$ and $\mathbb{K}^{per}$ is the perfect closure of a field $\mathbb{K}$. Combined with results about classification of finite subgroups of the group of biregular automorphisms of $S$, this gives a classification of finite subgroups of the group of birational automorphisms of $S$.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra Sonina

item.title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures IV-1: Obstructed and unobstructed foliated deformations
item.description: arXiv:2611.10069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study obstructions of deformations of foliated complex analytic structures. We describe obstructions in terms of Cech resolutions. From foliated complex analytic families in Part I and unfolded complex analytic families in Part III, we deduce the integrability conditions. We identify infinitesimal deformations and obstructions in terms of Dolbeault resolutions or Dolbeault type bicomplexes from the integrability conditions. Then we describe the correspondences of infinitesimal deformations and obstructions between Cech resolutions, and Dolbeault resolutions or Dolbeault type bicomplexes.
item.dc:creator: Chunghoon Kim

item.title: Adaptive visualization for enumerative problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.10131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an adaptive visualization framework and its implementation in the julia package AdaptiveVisualization.jl. Our algorithm visualizes functions using an adaptive sampling procedure that concentrates the evaluation budget at interesting regions of the domain. We illustrate our package on our main application: visualizing parameter spaces of enumerative problems.
item.dc:creator: Taylor Brysiewicz, Noah Vale

item.title: Automorphisms of Kummer and Artin-Schreier curves defined by Chebyshev polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.10255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let phi_m be the monic Chebyshev polynomial characterized by phi_m(t + t^-1) = t^m + t^-m. We study the geometric automorphism groups of the smooth projective models of y^n = phi_m(x) and y^p - y = phi_m(x). We classify the hyperelliptic family in genus at least two, in characteristic zero and odd characteristic. For every m >= 5, with p not dividing m in positive characteristic, we determine the projective stabilizer of the roots of phi_m together with infinity. For tame Kummer covers, we describe the normalizer of the cyclic deck group and compute it explicitly for m >= 6. It is the full group when m > 2n. If m >= 3 and n > 2m, the full group has order 2n in characteristic zero and in every characteristic prime to 2nm. The proof uses the dihedral Galois closure of the map to the y-line and Dickson's subgroup classification. In odd characteristic, we also classify all Artin-Schreier curves in the family with genus at least two. For m >= 3 prime to p >= 5, the group has order 2p. In characteristic three, exactly five degrees are exceptional. We give the groups and their actions, and treat the quadratic cases separately.
item.dc:creator: Ahmad Kazemifard, Saeed Tafazolian

item.title: Metric nefness of direct image sheaves under weakly semi-stable K\"ahler morphisms
item.description: arXiv:2611.10391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the nefness of the direct image sheaves of relative adjoint bundles under weakly semi-stable K\"ahler morphisms between complex spaces. We show that the direct image sheaves are locally free and that their tautological line bundles are metrically nef, strengthening the previously known results on torsion-freeness and certain weak positivity.
item.dc:creator: Osamu Fujino, Shigeharu Takayama

item.title: Birational Geometry of K-Moduli Spaces of Genus Four Curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.10415v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the wall-crossings for K-moduli spaces of (3,3)-curves on $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$. Together with the boundary polarized Calabi--Yau moduli space, these spaces interpolate between the GIT moduli space of (3,3)-curves and the Baily--Borel compactification of the moduli space of K3 surfaces arising as cyclic triple covers of $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$ branched along such curves. As applications, we describe the corresponding birational models in the Hassett--Keel--Looijenga program and realize the K-moduli space of degree one del Pezzo surfaces through explicit wall-crossings.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Ascher, Kristin DeVleming, Hongyu Luo, Yuchen Liu, Junyan Zhao

item.title: Extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces without Gaussian maps and classification of prime Fano threefolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.10426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In arXiv:2409.03960 an approach to the question of extendability of projective varieties via degeneration to ribbons was introduced, and in arXiv:2503.12661 it was used to give a new proof of optimal results on the extendability of general non-prime $K3$ surfaces and the classification of non-prime Fano threefolds. In this article we treat the prime case. We give a new proof of the optimal results on the extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces of every genus, of the classification of prime Fano threefolds of Picard rank one due to Fano, Iskovskikh and Mukai, and of the irreducibility of their Hilbert schemes. This involves degenerations of $K3$ surfaces to ribbons on embedded rational normal scrolls, called $K3$ carpets. We compute exactly the cohomology of the twisted normal bundle of these $K3$ carpets, instead of computing coranks of Gaussian maps of the canonical curve sections. The key challenge is to analyze the coboundary map of the sequence relating the normal bundle of the $K3$ carpet to the normal bundle of the scroll. We give a deformation theoretic interpretation of this map. Given such a $K3$ carpet and its hyperplane section, which is a canonical ribbon, we show that the coboundary map corresponds to the obstruction to lifting a first order deformation of the underlying scroll fixing the underlying rational normal curve to a first order deformation of the $K3$ carpet fixing the canonical ribbon. To compute the obstruction, we use a result on extensions of non-split ribbons on any curve to a unique $K$-trivial carpet in a canonical way.
item.dc:creator: Jayan Mukherjee, with an appendix written jointly with Anand Deopurkar

item.title: The moduli stack of affine bundles with fixed linearisation type
item.description: arXiv:2611.10879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The goal of this article is the classification of affine bundles with fixed linearisation type over a compact complex manifold $X$. More precisely, let $E$ be a fixed holomorphic vector bundle over $X$ and $\mathcal{E}$ the associated locally free sheaf. We will assume that there exists an effective divisor $D$ on $X$ such that $H^1(X,\mathcal{E}(D))=0$. This condition is always satisfied when $X$ is a projective complex manifold. We define in a natural way the moduli stack of affine bundles on $X$ whose linearisation is isomorphic to $E$, and we prove that this moduli stack is isomorphic to the quotient stack $\big[H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D)_D)/H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D))\ltimes \mathrm{Aut}(E)\big]$ of the complex vector space $H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D)_D)$ by the semi-direct product of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(E)$ (which is always an affine algebraic group) by the complex vector space $H^0(X,{\cal E}(D))$. Our isomorphism is obtained by constructing explicitly comparison functors $\mathscr{A}$, $\mathscr{T}$ between the two stacks and explicit natural isomorphisms $\mathscr{A}\circ\mathscr{T}\stackrel{\simeq}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{id}$, $\mathrm{id} \stackrel{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\mathscr{T}\circ\mathscr{A}$.
item.dc:creator: Naoufal Bouchareb, Andrei Teleman

item.title: Unramified case of Colliot-Th\'el\`ene conjecture on quadratic forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.10978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Colliot-Th\'el\`ene conjecture on quadratic forms asserts that any rationally isotropic nondegenerate quadratic form over a semilocal regular domain with $2$ invertible is isotropic. We prove the Colliot-Th\'el\`ene conjecture for semilocal regular domains that are geometrically regular over a discrete valuation ring with $2$ invertible. In particular, this includes unramified regular local rings of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, where $p\neq 2$.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Panin, Ivan Gaidai-Turlov

item.title: A Lefschetz Alternative for Real Characters on Smooth Quasi-Projective Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.11195v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a Lefschetz alternative for real characters on smooth complex quasi-projective varieties, extending Simpson's classical theorem beyond the compact K\"ahler setting. More precisely, for a nonzero real character of the fundamental group of a smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety, either the character factors through a holomorphic fibration onto a Riemann orbifold with connected general fiber, or every level set of an associated primitive function on the corresponding covering is connected and its inclusion induces a surjection onto the fundamental group of the covering. Our approach combines logarithmic holomorphic $1$-forms with a geometric flow construction to overcome the difficulties arising from noncompactness. Meanwhile, we prove a quasi-projective analogue of the Napier--Ramachandran theorem, showing that an epimorphism onto $\Z $ whose kernel is not finitely generated must factor through a hyperbolic Riemann orbifold. As applications, we derive several new restrictions on the structure of quasi-projective groups.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Liu

item.title: Finite torsion in Hodge--Witt cohomology groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.11269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a bounded coherent complex of graded modules over the Raynaud ring $R$, we compare three descriptions of finite torsion: Ekedahl's pieces $A_f^2$ and $A_{\SSpart}^1$ of the biduality filtration, the nilpotent and semisimple parts of the torsion of the Illusie--Raynaud c\oe ur, and the corresponding parts of the finite torsion $t^1$ of Ekedahl's diagonal cohomology. We show that finite torsion in bidegree $(0,i+1)$ measures the failure of the $i$th flat Artin--Mazur formal group to be smooth; we deduce that all flat Artin--Mazur formal groups of a Mazur--Ogus variety are smooth. For a smooth projective surface, we identify the three possible dual pairs in terms of the $p$-primary torsion of the geometric N\'eron--Severi group and the local-local and local-\'etale parts of the finite Picard quotient.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Yang

item.title: All-genus mirror symmetry for the type-$D$ minimal resolution Calabi-Yau threefold
item.description: arXiv:2611.11300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $Y$ be the product of a minimal resolution of a binary dihedral surface singularity with an equivariant line, with volume-preserving scalar action. We identify its stable equivariant descendant Gromov--Witten theory and its free energies in genus at least two with the sign-sector topological recursion of the degenerate type-$D$ relativistic Toda spectral curve. The $R-$matrix calibration is determined at a partial large-radius limit, where the trivalent exceptional curve retains a nonzero K\"ahler parameter, while the remaining parameters vanish. The limiting theory on the mirror side is a sum of twisted point theories and the local $(-2,0)$ curve theory. Moreover, we identify the equivariant K-group supported on the surface zero section with an integral relative homology group of the mirror. Explicit cycles for the dual tautological bundles realize their Gamma central charges and all stable Gamma-framed descendants.
item.dc:creator: Bohan Fang, Zhuoming Lan

item.title: Classification of 3-dimensional complex nilmanifolds - Teichm\"uller and moduli spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.11407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify complex nilmanifolds of dimension three by describing the Teichm\"uller and moduli spaces of left-invariant complex structures for every real six-dimensional nilmanifold.
item.dc:creator: Konstantin Wehler

item.title: Derived invariance of the space of holomorphic two-forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.11708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Phi:D^b(X)\to D^b(Y)$ be a derived equivalence between smooth projective complex varieties, and let $h=c_1(L)$ for an ample line bundle $L$ on $X$. For $z\in\mathbb{C}$, transporting the cup-product action and evaluating at $e^{zh}$ gives a homomorphism of graded algebras $\Theta^\bullet_{F,z}:H^\bullet(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\to H^\bullet(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $F$ is the cohomological transform of $\Phi$. We prove that $\Theta^\bullet_{F,i}$ is an isomorphism in degrees one and two. In particular, $X$ and $Y$ have the same number of holomorphic two-forms. The proof in degree two uses the Hodge-Riemann bilinear relations on $X$ and on $X\times X$. We also prove derived invariance of all Hodge numbers when $K_X$ is trivial and the conjugate of a holomorphic volume form belongs to the subalgebra of $H^\bullet(X,\mathcal O_X)$ generated in degrees one and two. In even dimension, the evaluation isomorphism allows us to compare the ranks of cup product by powers of symplectic two-forms on the Hochschild diagonals. These ranks determine the Hodge numbers individually.
item.dc:creator: Roland Abuaf

item.title: Zero-cycles on quotients of multiple double covers and their products
item.description: arXiv:2611.11829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the 0-cycle form of the generalized Bloch conjecture for smooth projective models of subgroup quotients of multiple double covers of projective space, with smooth branch hypersurfaces and reduced simple normal crossings branch divisor. Our integral character criterion yields, in every dimension at least four, simply connected varieties of general type with 0-cycle Chow group \(\mathbb{Z}\), canonical volume four, and no birational product decomposition. We also determine optimal integral supports for componentwise product quotients and character decompositions of degree zero Chow groups. Within this covering class, we classify the minimum volume models and compute their pluricanonical map degrees.
item.dc:creator: Wenchuan Hu

item.title: Gersten resolutions for logarithmic forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.11933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth variety over a field $k$ of characteristic 0. We show that (two versions of) the Zariski sheaves of regular $k$-linear logarithmic differential forms on $X$ (in the most na\"{\i}ve sense, i.e. sums of products of logarithmic differentials) have Gersten property (and therefore coincide). It turns out that the values of these sheaves are free abelian groups. As a consequence, for any integer $n>0$, these sheaves modulo $n$ also have Gersten property. The proof is an elementary application of the Voevodsky's $(-1)$-machinery and consists of assembling several well-known results.
item.dc:creator: M. Rovinsky

item.title: Generalizations of Igusa surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.12201v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a criterion for the contracted product $E \times^G X$ to have a singular Picard scheme, where $E$ is an elliptic curve, $G \subset E$ is a finite subgroup scheme, and $X$ is a projective $G$-normal curve, in the sense of Brion. We show that every smooth projective surface with a singular Picard scheme and a positive-dimensional automorphism group scheme arises in this way. We also illustrate the criterion by constructing two new families of surfaces with singular Picard schemes, arising from $G$-normal curves $X$ for $G = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $G = \boldsymbol{\alpha}_p$, respectively. As a special case of $G = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, we recover Igusa's classical example. Finally, we compute all infinitesimal group schemes which appear as $\operatorname{Pic}^0_S/(\operatorname{Pic}^0_S)_{\mathrm{red}}$ for all (quasi)-bielliptic surfaces $S$. This completes the description of the singular Picard schemes of smooth projective surfaces of Kodaira dimension zero.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Fong, Matilde Maccan, Ludvig Modin

item.title: The rank of the Fano normal function via the Fermat cubic
item.description: arXiv:2611.12276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the canonical derivative of the Fano normal function has rank ten at the Fermat cubic threefold. This yields a direct proof of its generic maximal rank, a result also implied by a general theorem of Gao--Zhang. Our approach combines Hain's equivariance principle with an explicit representation-theoretic computation and the nonvanishing of the Griffiths infinitesimal invariant established by Collino--Naranjo--Pirola.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Fassina

item.title: Sharp minima of higher Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated singularities
item.description: arXiv:2611.12289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the minimum higher Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated complex polynomial singularities with fixed ambient dimension and multiplicity. A Fermat polynomial of multiplicity $m$, perturbed by the $(m+1)$-st power of a linear form, attains both minimum sequences at every order. These values remain the minima at each prescribed total degree $d>m$; the homogeneous case $d=m$ has a separate Tjurina formula. The proof expresses the Tjurina defect through multiplication in the filtered Milnor algebra and uses the monomial strong Lefschetz theorem to attain the resulting rank bound. We also determine the associated graded higher Tjurina algebras of this family and show that they are unchanged by terms of order at least $m+2$.
item.dc:creator: Chuangqiang Hu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Lishan Yu, Huaiqing Zuo

item.title: Cylindricity of log del Pezzo surfaces in characteristic five
item.description: arXiv:2611.12341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic five, we prove that a log del Pezzo surface of Picard rank one contains no cylinder if it is not log liftable. We also characterize Du Val del Pezzo surfaces that contain no cylinder in positive characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Dae-Won Lee, Masaru Nagaoka, Masatomo Sawahara

item.title: Lipschitz inner rates of normal surface singularities
item.description: arXiv:2611.12380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we connect the local Lipschitz geometry of a normal surface singularity with a rational homology sphere link to the analytic semigroup $S_{an}(\tilde{X})$ associated with a convenient resolution. Under certain restriction, we provide an explicit computational characterization of the Lipschitz rate $q_v$ associated with an irreducible exceptional curve $E_v$ in terms of the semigroup. We also show that removing the restriction we get examples when $q_v$ cannot be determined from the semigroup. Interestingly enough, this phenomenon already happens for rational singularities. Indeed, we exemplify that the inner rates of rational singularities are not topological.
item.dc:creator: J\'anos Nagy, Andr\'as N\'emethi

item.title: Derivations tangent to polar discriminants
item.description: arXiv:2611.12413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe the module of logarithmic derivations along the discriminant of a stable polar representation of a reductive algebraic group. It splits into derivations along the fibres of the quotient map and a free summand lifted from logarithmic derivations along the associated branch divisor. This gives a uniform extension of previous results on full adjoint discriminants. We prove that, for visible stable polar actions of semisimple groups with finite generic stabilizer, the discriminant is a free divisor. For stable periodic gradings of arbitrary order with semisimple degree-zero group, we construct explicit Saito matrices from the infinitesimal action and the gradients of basic invariants, which yields determinantal equations for several exceptional discriminants. In particular, starting with exceptional Lie algebras, we provide examples of free discriminants of degrees 60, 120, 126 and 240 for inner gradings and a degree-72 example for an outer one.
item.dc:creator: Vladimiro Benedetti (UniCA,LJAD), Daniele Faenzi (UBE,IMB), Simone Marchesi (UB)

item.title: $\lambda_g$-Integrals on triple, one-part admissible covers
item.description: arXiv:2611.12450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We effectively compute all intersection numbers of the form $\lambda_g\psi^d$ on moduli spaces of genus $g$ admissible covers with one point of full ramification and two additional branch points with arbitrary profile. We encode these invariants in appropriate generating functions, which we relate to the Hamiltonians of the KdV hierarchy.
item.dc:creator: Renzo Cavalieri, David Klompenhouwer, Paolo Rossi

item.title: Semisimple Deformations of Contraction Algebras for Smooth Threefold Flops
item.description: arXiv:2611.12490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building on Bryan--Katz--Leung, Hua--Toda and Kawamata, we study deformations of contraction algebras and the local geometry of the scheme of associative algebra laws. Let $A$ be the basic contraction algebra of a completed projective flopping contraction of a smooth complex threefold. We construct a finite free polynomial family that is constant and semisimple away from the origin, with the original curve projectors fixed. For each restricted positive root $\beta=(\beta_i)$, with coordinates indexed by the retained vertices, the split generic fibre has $n_\beta$ matrix blocks of size $\sum_i\beta_i$, and the labelled projector $e_i$ has rank $\beta_i$ on each block. Here $n_\beta$ is the corresponding genus-zero Gopakumar--Vafa invariant. If the geometric generic fibre of a finite free associative formal deformation of $A$ is semisimple, it has the same matrix factors, and any lifts of the original projectors have the same ranks on those factors. The scheme of associative algebra laws is smooth at $A$. The closure of the corresponding semisimple orbit is its unique irreducible component through $A$. The proof uses the curve divisors of Katz--Morrison and Nabijou--Wemyss, presentations of the universal contraction quotient and its cocenter, and the orbit method of Jelisiejew--Smoktunowicz. These presentations prove the geometric Hua--Toda flatness assertions. In the geometric families considered here, the relative contraction algebra, its centre and its cocenter are finite free over arbitrary complete Noetherian local complex bases. On a smooth open neighbourhood of $A$ in the scheme of algebra laws, the centres and cocenters form dual vector bundles compatible with arbitrary base change. For the type $D$ algebras $D_{n,2}$ with $n\ge2$, the centre morphism gives counterexamples to the smoothness assertion in Conjecture 1.4(2) of Jelisiejew--Smoktunowicz.
item.dc:creator: Shutao Bi

item.title: On the Cohomological Amplitude of the Locally Analytic Jacquet--Langlands Functor
item.description: arXiv:2611.12608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a local cohomological bound $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)\in D^{[0,\dim X]}$ for a pro-\'etale sheaf with a derived $p$-complete integral lattice whose modulo $p^m$ reductions are filtered colimits of finite local systems on an affinoid topologically of finite type over $C$. For $G=\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, with $n\geq2$ and $F/\mathbb Q_p$ finite, we apply these local bounds to variants of Scholze's Jacquet--Langlands functor $\mathrm{JL}_\mathscr{B}(\Pi):= R\Gamma_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(\mathbb{P}^{n-1}_C,\mathcal{F}_{\Pi}\otimes^{L, \square}_{\mathbb{Q}_p}\mathscr{B})$ for $\mathscr{B}\in\{\mathbb{Q}_p, \widehat{\mathscr{O}}, \mathbb{B}_J\}$ and Banach or compact-type LB representations $\Pi$ of $G$, obtaining $\mathrm{JL}_{\mathscr{B}}(\Pi)\in D^{[0,2(n-1)]}$ for each choice of $\mathscr{B}$. We also prove that for arbitrary continuous principal series $I(\eta)=(\mathrm{Ind}_B^G\eta)^{\mathrm{cont}}$, we have $\mathrm{JL}(\mathrm{Ind}_B^G\eta)\in D^{[0, n]}$, while $\mathrm{JL}_{\widehat{\mathscr{O}}}(I(\eta)),\mathrm{JL}_{\mathbb{B}_J}(I(\eta))\in D^{[0, n-1]}$.
item.dc:creator: Yu Xiao

item.title: Counter-examples to Conjectures on NCCRs via a Reductive McKay Correspondence
item.description: arXiv:2611.12679v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We disprove three conjectures appearing in Van den Bergh's plenary ICM survey, posed by De Deyn and Van den Bergh, which concern the interplay between non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs) and the stringy Euler characteristic. Our counter-examples are applications of a new McKay correspondence for reductive groups that we prove in this paper, extending the classical McKay correspondence for finite groups. We obtain explicit formulas for the stringy $E$-functions of reductive quotients in terms of the Weyl group action and stringy $E$-functions of toric varieties; we also obtain an equivalent formula expressed as an integral of the age function over Weyl-fixed loci of a compact real torus. For symmetric representations, our expressions are related to arithmetic Tutte polynomials, yielding combinatorial formulas for the stringy Euler characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Satriano, Jeremy Usatine

item.title: Fourteenth-canonical birationality of threefolds with positive geometric genus
item.description: arXiv:2611.12717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the pluricanonical map of a complex projective threefold of general type with canonical singularities and positive geometric genus is birational in every degree at least fourteen. The bound is sharp.
item.dc:creator: Zhengjie Yu

item.title: Perfect loops of proper schemes
item.description: arXiv:2611.12719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the perfect loop space $LX$ of a proper scheme $X$ over a local field $F$. We show that if $X$ contains a rational curve, then $LX$ is not ind-representable, even in a very weak sense. We also show that if $X$ admits a proper model $\mathfrak{X}$ over the integers $\mathcal{O}$ of $F$, whose geometric special fiber does not contain rational curves, then $L^+\mathfrak{X} \stackrel{\sim}{\to} LX$ is an isomorphism via the natural map, where $L^+\mathfrak{X}$ denotes the perfect positive loop space (jet scheme) of $\mathfrak{X}$. In particular, $LX$ is a scheme in this case.
item.dc:creator: Alexander B. Ivanov

item.title: Semiampleness of Hodge line bundles and b-semiampleness of the moduli part
item.description: arXiv:2611.12744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give proofs of Hodge semiampleness and b-semiampleness without using o-minimality. We establish a geometric semiampleness criterion for line bundles on proper algebraic spaces. Let $(X,D)$ be a log smooth pair with $X$ a proper algebraic space. For an integral polarizable pure variation of Calabi--Yau type on $X\setminus D$ with unipotent local monodromy, let $L$ be its extended highest Hodge line. If $L$ is numerically integrable and has torsion combinatorial monodromy, then $L$ is semiample. We also prove semiampleness of extended Griffiths lines. We construct normal projective period compactifications on which a positive power of the Griffiths line extends to an ample line bundle. As an application, we prove that the moduli b-divisor $\mathbf{M}$ of a projective lc-trivial fibration over a normal algebraic variety is b-semiample, provided that the generic boundary is effective. Suppose further that the geometric generic pair is klt and its boundary is big, with nonzero coefficients in a fixed finite set $I\subset(0,1)\cap\mathbb{Q}$. Then $c\mathbf{M}$ is b-Cartier and b-free for an integer $c>0$ depending only on the relative dimension and $I$. We extend b-semiampleness to analogous projective fibrations over normal complex analytic bases, assuming a global relative polarization and an invertible log pluricanonical sheaf pulled back from the base.
item.dc:creator: Zhengyu Hu, Kefeng Liu, Yang Shen

item.title: Functorial Homological Mirror Symmetry for Acyclic Cluster Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.12751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the formalism of cluster models, a class of log Calabi-Yau varieties obtained from smooth quasi-affine toric varieties by iterated affine blowups along non-toric codimension 2 centers determined by a really full rank quiver. Cluster models include the truncated cluster varieties of Gross, Hacking, and Keel with respect to really full rank quivers, all really full rank acyclic cluster varieties, and all open toric subvarieties of $\mathbb{C}^n\times(\mathbb{C}^*)^m$. We then construct mirrors to cluster models via iterated Weinstein handle attachments to toric mirrors, so that the corresponding skeleta acquire compact pieces, and we prove homological mirror symmetry for all cluster models, compatibly with freezing, deleting, and contracting vertices of the quiver. This extends toric mirror symmetry and its naturalities beyond the cotangent bundle. In particular, we obtain homological mirror symmetry for all really full rank acyclic cluster varieties. We develop this package with a view towards conjectures of Marsh, Rietsch, and Williams about mirror symmetry for Grassmannians and closed positroid varieties. Motivated by these, we also conjecture that open positroid varieties are self-mirror. Assuming a natural ansatz, we prove this for a class of positroid varieties that includes nontrivial cells in every Grassmannian and all cells in finite-type Grassmannians. Towards this end we introduce a new combinatorial input, the notion of weak $k$-booleanness for permutations and braids.
item.dc:creator: Josephine Hlavinka

item.title: The Minimum Canonical Volume of Threefolds of General Type
item.description: arXiv:2611.12786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the sharp lower bound $vol(X) \geq 1/420$ for every smooth complex projective threefold $X$ of general type.
item.dc:creator: Pinxian Bie, Peien Du, Zhengjie Yu

item.title: Motivic Mirror Symmetry for Sink-recurrent Cluster Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.12863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove motivic mirror symmetry for full-rank sink-recurrent cluster varieties. We allow skew-symmetrizable principal parts and invert all frozen variables. The rational geometric motive of such a variety is isomorphic to the additive orbifold motive of the mirror stack of Hu and Shende. This gives comparisons of cohomology, higher Chow groups, and algebraic $K$-theory with rational coefficients. The proof combines quantum deformation with the splitting of these motives into Tate summands. For really full-rank skew-symmetric seeds, a finite \'{e}tale morphism realizes the comparison. We also study this geometric comparison in families over the projective line.
item.dc:creator: Haoyang Liu, Tianle Liu

item.title: Motivic generating functions and $L$-derivatives of cohomological automorphic representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.10478v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Forty years ago, Gross and Zagier proved a remarkable formula computing the central derivative of the Rankin--Selberg $L$-function of a cusp form $f$ of weight $2$ and a character of the class group of an imaginary quadratic field, satisfying the so-called Heegner condition, and deduce that the nonvanishing of the central derivative implies the nonvanishing of the corresponding Mordell--Weil rank. This formula was later generalized in various contexts and degrees, for example, by S. Zhang for $f$ of higher even weights; and by Yuan--Zhang--Zhang for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form of parallel weight $2$ over an arbitrary totally real field $F$ and $\chi$ a Dirichlet character of an arbitrary CM extension $E/F$, allowing arbitrary ramification. In this article, we prove a Gross--Zagier type formula in the context of doubling method, for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form over $F$ and $\chi$ a Hecke character of $E$ of general weights under a balancing condition, again allowing arbitrary ramification. Indeed, we even formulate a general conjecture which we call the motivic arithmetic inner product formula, for cohomological automorphic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_{2r}$ over $E$ of hermitian type of balanced weights.
item.dc:creator: Yifeng Liu

item.title: Multivariate Pellarin $L$-values on algebraic curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.10495v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a generating trace formula for multicharacter ideal-type $L$-values associated with rank-one Drinfeld modules. For a sign-normalized Hayes module with free period lattice, the formula realizes the $L$-values at weights $n\equiv s\pmod{q^{\deg_\infty}-1}$ as a trace over the ordinary Hilbert class field. We further characterize the polynomials in the exponential variable $X$ arising in multicharacter lattice generating identities over arbitrary function rings. Their coefficients are given explicitly via the shtuka basis, which gives concrete control over their supports and degrees. This completely settles an open problem of Pellarin and Perkins: these polynomials are all constant if and only if $s<2q$. The results on coefficients apply to curves of arbitrary genus, infinite places of arbitrary degree, and nonprincipal period lattices.
item.dc:creator: Chuangqiang Hu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Lishan Yu

item.title: Dominant permutations, positive mixed-variable formulas, and product-splitting equivalence for (double) Schubert polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.10953v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present new positive combinatorial formulas for triple Schubert coefficients in mixed-variable products of double Schubert polynomials, $\mathfrak{S}_u(x;y)\mathfrak{S}_v(x;z)$, expressed in the $\mathfrak{S}_w(x;y)$ basis, in the case where $u$ is dominant. This result complements earlier results where $v$ was assumed dominant. To generalize further, we introduce a relation on permutations that we call ``domination,'' under which dominant permutations dominate all others. When $u$ dominates $w$, we obtain an explicit positive formula for $c^w_{u,v}(y;z)$, which in particular yields positivity when $u$ and $v$ have separated descents. In addition to these new positivity results, we establish a product--splitting equivalence for double Schubert polynomials, relating triple Schubert coefficients to splitting coefficients. This equivalence highlights structural symmetries and provides reduction methods for computing coefficients that are otherwise difficult to access. Taken together, these results extend the range of double Schubert polynomial products for which positivity can be established combinatorially and yield explicit formulas that can be implemented computationally.
item.dc:creator: Matthew J. Samuel

item.title: Twisted pencils of quartics, braid monodromy factorizations, and non-Hopfian Hurwitz curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.11092v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study which groups arise as fundamental groups of complements of affine Hurwitz curves. In every such group the product of the meridians is central and maps to the vector of component degrees in homology; this rules out, for instance, the Baumslag-Solitar groups $\operatorname{BS}(p,q)$ with $\lvert p\rvert\neq\lvert q\rvert$, and the groups of links with at least two components and vanishing linking numbers. O. V. Kulikova circumvented this obstruction for $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)$ by passing to the non-Hopfian group $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)\times\mathbb{Z}$, which Vik. S. Kulikov's doubling algorithm realizes in degree $768$. We give an explicit braid monodromy factorization of degree 12 with this group. The corresponding curve is not isotopic to an algebraic curve, yet it is obtained from a union of three quartics in a pencil by a single twist along a circle. More generally, for every closed braid $\hat\beta$ we realize $\pi_1(S^3\setminus\hat\beta)\times\mathbb{Z}$ by an explicit Hurwitz curve, again a twist of a union of quartics in a pencil. In the other direction, a Hurwitz curve with group $\operatorname{BS}(k,k+1)\times\mathbb{Z}$ has degree at least $4$, as every Hurwitz curve consisting of a conic and a line is H-isotopic to an algebraic one, after separation of its critical points. Finally, we show that certain semiholomorphic germs, among them those realizing the generalized Borromean rings, are braided surfaces but not Hurwitz curve germs.
item.dc:creator: Alexander I. Suciu

item.title: Bott--Chern and Aeppli Cohomology of toroidal groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.11184v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups of theta toroidal groups in arbitrary dimensions, obtaining explicit dimension formulas and bases in all bidegrees. For general toroidal groups, we determine the Hausdorff reductions of these cohomology groups and show that they coincide with those of theta toroidal groups. We also compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups themselves in certain specific bidegrees, without passing to their Hausdorff reductions.
item.dc:creator: Xiaojun Wu

item.title: New families of maximal curves not covered by the Hermitian curve and their cyclic automorphism groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.11298v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every prime power $q>2$, integer $n\ge2$ and $1\le r\le 2n-1$, we construct an $\mathbb F_{q^{2n}}$-maximal curve $T_{q,n,r}$ with Kummer equation \[ z^{q^n+1}=\eta^{-R}y(1-y^{q-1})^R, \qquad \frac{q^r-1}{q-1},\] where $\eta\in\mathbb F_{q^{2n}}^*$ satisfies $\eta^{q^n}=-\eta$. For fixed $q,n$, these are cyclic covers of the projective line over a single field, indexed by the integer $r$. Writing $\delta=\gcd(q^n+1,R)$, we prove that the genus is $(q-1)(q^n+1-\delta)/2$ and that $T_{q,n,r}$ is covered by the Hermitian curve $\mathcal H_{q^n}$ over an algebraic closure if and only if $\min(r,2n-r)$ divides $n$. For $1<r<n$ and $\delta=1$, the full automorphism group is cyclic of order $(q-1)(q^n+1)$, and distinct values of $r$ give curves that are nonisomorphic over an algebraic closure despite having the same genus and full automorphism group. We also give explicit equations and genera for all their Galois subfields. When $n\ge 4$ is a power of two, this produces families over a fixed field whose members are not covered by $\mathcal H_{q^n}$.
item.dc:creator: Xubin Hu, Liming Ma, Yipeng Wang

item.title: Simple algebraic groups with good reduction, the genus problem, and unramified cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2611.11631v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We obtain a number of new results on the arithmetic of linear algebraic groups over higher-dimensional fields. In particular, we resolve some key open questions over 2-dimensional global fields, such as the finiteness of the genus of spinor groups of quadratic forms of dimension $\geq 10$. We also extend various finiteness results to new classes of fields, including function fields of $p$-adic surfaces. Our arguments rely in a crucial way on new finiteness results for unramified cohomology.
item.dc:creator: Igor A. Rapinchuk

item.title: On sinks and mirrors
item.description: arXiv:2611.11660v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a full rank sink recurrent cluster $\mathcal{A}$ variety, we prove that its wrapped Fukaya category is equivalent to the category of coherent sheaves on a stacky elaboration of the dual Fock-Goncharov cluster $\mathcal{X}$ variety. In particular, braid varieties for a semisimple group are mirror to the braid varieties for the Langlands dual group. Another example: for compact surfaces with no interior marked points, a least one marked point on each boundary component, and at least two marked points in total, the Fock-Goncharov moduli for SL(2) and PGL(2) are homologically mirror. The results were obtained in communion with ChatGPT Astra.
item.dc:creator: Mingyuan Hu, Vivek Shende

item.title: Binary Belief Propagation Fixed Points: Finiteness, Rigidity, and Topological Complexity
item.description: arXiv:2611.11713v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A fixed finite binary Ising model has only finitely many admissible complex belief propagation fixed points, even at degenerate parameter values. Families of positive fixed points obtained by varying external fields can nevertheless have nontrivial topology. We study this distinction through the external-field projection. For a fixed field, we prove finiteness by bounding the pole orders of the magnetizations on a hypothetical complex solution curve. The generic degree on the support graph then bounds the total local multiplicity. A graph has a single smooth real line as its full positive response for every choice of positive couplings, base field, and strictly positive sweep direction exactly when it contains no two vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs of cycle rank at least two. Two such subgraphs suffice to create a circular component. For a plane obtained by varying two vertex fields, connected simple bipartite cubic graphs with one uniform coupling and a universal bound on the fixed fields realize every genus. The minimum number of vertices grows logarithmically in the genus, by a matching algebraic upper bound on Betti numbers. Finally, we certify the complete field discriminant of an eighteen-vertex product model and recover its torus component's genus from the counts of distinct roots on all field cells. The three main theorems, including the logarithmic size bounds, are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.
item.dc:creator: Yusuke Watanabe

item.title: Superlinear regularity of Frobenius powers on a normal hypersurface
item.description: arXiv:2611.12008v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give answers to four questions on linear bounds for Frobenius powers. Let $\mathfrak m$ denote the homogeneous maximal ideal. We construct a height-two prime $I$ in a geometrically normal four-dimensional graded hypersurface $R$ of characteristic two such that, for every power $q\geq16$ of four, the Loewy length of $H^0_{\mathfrak m}(R/I^{[q]})$ is at least $q^{3/2}/8-1$. Thus no fixed integer $C$ gives annihilation by $\mathfrak m^{Cq}$ for all $q$, as required by the Hochster--Huneke condition $(\mathrm{LC})$. The same construction gives superlinear lower bounds for the Castelnuovo--Mumford regularity in Katzman's question, for the exponents of the embedded primary components in the question of Smith and Swanson, and for the degree in the least variable in Katzman's Gr\"obner basis conjecture. The bounds follow from the degree of the kernel line bundle of a multiplication pencil associated to a family of plane quartics.
item.dc:creator: Tran Nam Trung, Hoang Le Truong

item.title: $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded norms for de Rham-Witt forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.12043v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We make two case studies of $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded homotopy in connection with $p$-adic cohomology. First, we identify the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf T)$-graded $\mathrm{TC}^-$ and $\mathrm{TP}$ of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings as multi-Rees algebras for the Nygaard and $\phi^\bullet(I)$-adic filtrations. We additionally compute $E^{h\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ and $E^{t\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ when $E$ is a general even $\mathbf E_\infty$-ring with $\mathbf T$-action, and compute $(\mathrm{TR}^n)^{h\mathbf T/C_{p^n}}_\bigstar$ in terms of iterated Nygaard filtrations. Next, we compute the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf Z_p)^\land$-graded $\mathrm{TR}$ of smooth algebras over a perfectoid base, providing a pushout of the works of Hesselholt and Angeltveit-Gerhardt along the base case $\mathbf F_p$. Using this, we extend Angeltveit's Norm map of Witt vectors to the de Rham-Witt complex, which participates in a "Witt coordinates" decomposition of the $p$-primary Adams operations.
item.dc:creator: Yuri J. F. Sulyma

item.title: Singularities in leaf closures on complex surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.12402v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a geometric and dynamical criterion excluding minimal sets contained in the regular locus of a holomorphic foliation on a compact complex surface. In particular, we prove that every Jouanolou foliation of degree at least two has no exceptional minimal set. We also give an explicit lower bound, growing linearly with the degree, for the number of singularities in every regular leaf closure of a Jouanolou foliation. This bound persists under small perturbations, as does the existence of a nonempty open saturated set whose leaves accumulate at all singularities. Under finite pullback unramified over the singular set, the bound is multiplied by the degree of the normalised component over the base leaf. Together with a general persistence theorem, this yields nonempty analytic open sets of foliations on every smooth projective surface with arbitrarily large uniform lower bounds on the number of singularities in their regular leaf closures. On double-plane K3 surfaces, we obtain foliations with ample canonical bundle and explicitly describe and count their singularities.
item.dc:creator: Mauricio Corr\^ea, Fernando Reis

item.title: Rigidity does not imply substitution rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2611.12590v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We obtain a negative answer to a question of Freudenburg concerning rigidity conditions for a polynomial. We construct a polynomial that does not lie in the kernel of any nonzero locally nilpotent derivation on the polynomial ring, but there exist an affine domain, algebraically independent elements and a locally nilpotent derivation such that the result of substituting elements into the polynomial lies in the kernel of that locally nilpotent derivation, but at least one of the substituted elements does not lie in that kernel.
item.dc:creator: Veronika Kikteva

item.title: When is Polynomial Optimization SoS-Exact? Sufficient Regularization and Strict Gram Representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.12697v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Global minimization of multivariate polynomials is computationally difficult in general, and nonnegativity does not necessarily imply a sum-of-squares (SoS) representation. We show that adding sufficiently strong Euclidean regularization to a polynomial provides a general mechanism for overcoming such challenges. Namely, for any multivariate polynomial $P$ of degree at most $p$ with a nonzero linear coefficient, and any even integer $2d>p$, we prove that $m_\sigma(s)=P(s)+\frac{\sigma}{2d}\|s\|_2^{2d}$ is SoS exact for all sufficiently large $\sigma$. Furthermore, the shifted polynomial $m_\sigma-\min m_\sigma$ admits a positive-definite Gram representation on appropriately-shifted nonconstant monomials. Consequently, the global minimum and minimizer can be recovered exactly by a single degree-$d$ semidefinite programming (SDP) representation, whose size is polynomial in the dimension for fixed $d$, without requiring higher levels of the SoS hierarchy. The proof develops a degree-independent mechanism based on the Bregman remainder of the regularizer: its strict Gram margin absorbs the lower-degree polynomial perturbations. We further establish an analogous exact SDP regime for polynomial optimization over sufficiently small Euclidean balls, connecting large regularization with small-radius trust-region problems. Finally, we investigate how the algebraic structure of the regularizer governs the existence of a strict Gram margin, extending the mechanism beyond Euclidean norms while identifying limitations of coordinate-separable regularization.
item.dc:creator: Coralia Cartis, Wenqi Zhu

item.title: Derived invariance of the numbers $h^{0,p}(X)$
item.description: arXiv:1907.08721v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be derived equivalent smooth projective varieties over the field of complex numbers. We prove that the numbers $h^{0,p}(X_1)$ and $h^{0,p}(X_2)$ are equal for any $p$.
item.dc:creator: Roland Abuaf

item.title: Metric Multiview Geometry---a Catalogue in Low Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2402.00648v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We systematically compile an exhaustive catalogue of multiview varieties and anchored multiview varieties arising from projections of points, lines, and planes in 1, 2, and 3-dimensional projective spaces. We say that two such varieties are ED-equivalent if there is a linear isomorphism between them that preserves ED-critical points. This gives rise to fourteen representatives, at most two of which are equivalent, and we determine various properties---dimension, set-theoretic equations, and multidegrees---for all varieties featured in our catalogue. In the case of points, we also present a complementary study of resectioning varieties and their singular loci. Finally, we propose conjectures for the Euclidean distance degrees of all varieties appearing in our comprehensive compilation.
item.dc:creator: Timothy Duff, Felix Rydell

item.title: Highest weight category structures on $rep(B)$ and full exceptional collections on generalized flag varieties over $\mathbb Z$
item.description: arXiv:2407.13653v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a split simply connected semi-simple algebraic group scheme $\mathbb G$ over $\mathbb Z$, a split maximaltorus $\mathbb T$ in $\mathbb G$and a parabolic subgroup scheme $\mathbb P\supset \mathbb T$, this paper constructs semi-orthogonal decompositions of the bounded derived category $D^b(rep(\mathbb P))$ of noetherian representations of $\mathbb P$ with each semi-orthogonal component being equivalent to the bounded derived category $D^b(rep(\mathbb G))$ of noetherian representations of $\mathbb G$. The semi-orthogonal components of those decompositions are stable under the monoidal action of $D^b(rep(\mathbb G))$ on $D^b(rep(\mathbb P))$. The decompositions depend on an arbitrarily chosen total order on the Weyl group that refines the Bruhat order. The semi-orthogonal decompositions are also compatible with the Bruhat order on cosets of the Weyl group of $\mathbb P$ in the Weyl group of $\mathbb G$. Their construction builds upon the foundational results on $\mathbb B$-modules from the works of Mathieu, Polo, and van der Kallen, and upon properties of the Steinberg basis of the $\mathbb T$-equivariant $K$-theory of $\mathbb G/\mathbb B$. As a corollary, we obtain full exceptional collections in the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on generalized flag schemes $\mathbb G/\mathbb P$ over $\mathbb Z$.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Samokhin, Wilberd van der Kallen

item.title: Semihomogenous vector bundles, $\mathbb Q$-twisted sheaves, duality, and linear systems on abelian varieties
item.description: arXiv:2407.20646v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we point out the natural relation between $\mathbb Q$-twisted objects of the derived category of abelian varieties, cohomological rank functions, and semihomogeneous vector bundles. We apply this to two basic classes of objects, corresponding to each other via the Fourier-Mukai-Poincar\'e transform: positive twists of the ideal sheaf of one point and of the evaluation complexes of ample simple semihomogeneous vector bundles. This naturally leads to the introduction of $\mathbb Q^{\ge 0}$- graded section modules associated to line bundles on abelian varieties built by means of semihomogeneous vector bundles (containing the usual section rings). We prove a duality relation between such modules associated to dual polarizations, which is not visible at the level of the usual section rings. Other applications include formulas relating the thresholds of relevant cohomological rank functions appearing in this context. As a consequence we show a lower bound for the base point free threshold of a polarization in function of its type, and some obstructions to surjectivity of multiplication maps of global sections of certain line bundles.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: International Journal of Mathematics Vol. 37, No. 13 (2026) 2650070
item.dc:creator: Nelson Alvarado, Giuseppe Pareschi

item.title: Noncommutative Hourglasses I: On the Classification of Q-Fano 3-Folds of Gorenstein Index 2 via Derived Categories
item.description: arXiv:2501.17454v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In previous work, Takagi used the methods of solving the Sarkisov links by calculating the corresponding Diophantine equations and the construction of key varieties to give all possible classifications and some implementations of a class $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano 3-fold with Fano index 1/2 and at worst $(1, 1, 1)/2$ or QODP singularities. Firstly, we use a method different from Kawamata's work to give the derived category formulas for general weighted blow-up and Kawamata weighted blow-up. On this basis, we study the changing behavior of the derived category of Takagi's varieties under Sarkisov links. Finally, by studying non-commutative projections, we give exceptional collections on the derived category of Takagi's varieties and their corresponding geometric meanings.
item.dc:creator: Xingbang Hao

item.title: NC-smooth thickenings and Jacobians
item.description: arXiv:2505.04023v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that a bounded complex of coherent sheaves on an abelian variety A, whose Fourier-Mukai transform has support of dimension at most 1, extends to a perfect complex on the standard NC-smooth thickening of A and on the deformation quantization of any constant Poisson bracket on A. We discuss a related conjectural characterization of Jacobians in terms of NC-smooth thickenings.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Polishchuk

item.title: Algebraic cycles on some Fano varieties with Hodge structure of level one and of Calabi-Yau type
item.description: arXiv:2509.12186v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Chow groups and \'etale motivic cohomology groups of smooth complete intersections with Hodge structures of level one, classified by Deligne and Rapoport, with particular attention to fivefolds. We extend these results to an \'etale motivic context and recover an analogous finite-dimensionality in the sense of Kimura. We then turn to quartic double fivefolds, which are Fano fivefolds whose middle cohomology is numerically similar to that of a Calabi-Yau threefold. By means of cubic surfaces which are totally ramified along the branch locus, we prove the integral Hodge conjecture for all of them. We also show that the comparison maps between their Chow groups and \'etale Chow groups are isomorphisms except possibly in codimension three, where we describe the kernel and the cokernel in terms of Bloch-Ogus cohomology and, via a Sarkisov link, of the unramified cohomology of a cubic surface over the function field of $\mathbb{P}^3$.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Montero, Iv\'an Rosas-Soto

item.title: Dividends of the BKR Equivalence: Quantifying the Dichotomy for Skyscraper Sheaves
item.description: arXiv:2509.15825v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G\subset \mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb C)$ be a nontrivial finite abelian subgroup and let $\Psi \colon D^b_G(\mathbb{C}^3) \xrightarrow{\sim} D^b(G\operatorname{-}\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{C}^3))$ denote the Bridgeland--King--Reid equivalence. For every nontrivial character $\chi$ of $G$, the transform of the corresponding skyscraper sheaf at the origin has exactly one nonzero cohomology sheaf, in degree $0$ or $-1$. We study the proportion $\mathcal B_0$ of characters for which this degree is zero. Using derived Reid's recipe, we establish the sharp bounds $1/3\leq\mathcal B_0\leq1$. For isolated quotient singularities, the lower bound sharpens to $1/2$, and we exhibit an explicit family of cyclic quotients indexed by positive integers $m$ for which $\mathcal{B}_0 \to 1$ as $m \to \infty$. We show that $\mathcal B_0=1$ precisely when the fiber over the origin has dimension at most one, and relate $\mathcal B_0$ to the Picard rank of $G\operatorname{-}\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{C}^3)$ and the number of compact exceptional divisors of the resolution $G\operatorname{-}\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{C}^3)\rightarrow \mathbb{C}^3/G$. A theorem of Craw--Lin--Yamagishi translates these estimates into bounds for the coordinate facets of the $G$-Hilbert GIT chamber. We discuss how the proportion $\mathcal{B}_0$ adapts to non-abelian finite subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{C})$.
item.dc:creator: Boris Tsvelikhovskiy

item.title: New nonabelian Hodge graphs from twisted irregular connections
item.description: arXiv:2509.24861v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is known that any meromorphic connection on the Riemann sphere determines a finite diagram (a generalised graph, possibly with negative edge multiplicities), which is invariant under the Fourier-Laplace transform. If the connection has regular singularities at finite distance and an untwisted irregular singularity at infinity, the diagram is a supernova graph, and the quiver modularity theorem of Boalch/Hiroe-Yamakawa shows that the corresponding nonabelian Hodge moduli space contains the Nakajima quiver variety of the graph as an open subset. In this note, motivated by the question of classifying these nonabelian Hodge diagrams, we obtain a necessary condition satisfied by all (core) nonabelian Hodge diagrams, involving ultrametric inequalities. We use this to investigate the class of such diagrams that are graphs (without edge-loops nor negative multiplicities), as well as certain special classes of nonabelian Hodge graphs: we show that there exist nonabelian Hodge graphs beyond the setting of the quiver modularity theorem, and obtain characterisations of fission graphs and of simply-laced nonabelian Hodge graphs.
item.dc:creator: Jean Dou\c{c}ot

item.title: Generalized Divisors and Canonical Coarsening on Tame Deligne-Mumford Curves
item.description: arXiv:2510.16796v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study effective generalized divisors on reduced tame Deligne-Mumford curves over $\mathbb{C}$ satisfying $G_1$ and $S_2$. Canonical coarsening maps divisor ideals to coarse canonical lattices. We describe its fibres by exact intervals of equivariant lattices. For flat projective finite-quotient families of geometrically reduced Gorenstein curves over locally Noetherian bases, with finite constant groups and the stated relative-duality and base-change hypotheses, we construct projective invariant-Quot schemes for fixed canonical lattices with finite flat quotients and prescribed quotient representations. A nontrivial marked deformation preserves the coarse ring, normalization, conductor and entire fixed canonical fibre, while a length-four isotypic jet detects its parameter. We compute the full normalization and conductor correction after support restriction on an explicit rank-three chart. As a module, the correction splits into one surface and two line canonical modules, with a common grading shift. The corresponding square-zero algebra extension is nonsplit. The full source-support pair is compared through second order. Exact computational certificates accompany the proofs.
item.dc:creator: Minghua Dou

item.title: Kato's Ramification filtration via de Rham-Witt complex and applications
item.description: arXiv:2601.12177v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given an $F$-finite regular scheme $X$ of positive characteristic and a simple normal crossing divisor $E$ on $X$, we introduce a filtration on the de Rham--Witt complex $W_m\Omega^\bullet_{X\setminus E}$. When $X$ is the spectrum of a henselian discrete valuation ring $A$ with quotient field $K$, this extends the classical filtration on $W_m(K)$ due to Brylinski. We show that Kato's ramification filtration on $H^q_\et(X \setminus E, {\Q}/{\Z}(q-1))$ for $q \ge 1$ admits an explicit description in terms of the above filtration on the de Rham--Witt complex of $X \setminus E$. When $q =1$, this specializes to the results of Kato and Kerz--Saito. As applications, we construct a generalized version of Kato's refined Swan conductor for regular schemes, prove Lefschetz theorems for Kato's ramification filtrations for smooth projective varieties over $F$-finite fields, and prove Lefschetz and vanishing theorems for the Brauer group.
item.dc:creator: Amalendu Krishna, Subhadip Majumder

item.title: Hecke curves in Frobenius strata of moduli space of rank 2 vector bundles
item.description: arXiv:2602.09879v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field with characteristic $2$, and let $X$ be a smooth projective algebraic curve of genus $g \geqslant 2$ over $k$. Let $\mathcal{M}^s_X(2,\mathcal{L})$ be the moduli space of rank $2$ stable vector bundles with determinant $\mathcal{L}$ on $X$. The Frobenius stratification measures the instability of bundles in $\mathcal{M}^s_X(r,\mathcal{L})$ under pullback by the Frobenius map. We show that there exists a Frobenius stratum in $\mathcal{M}^s_X(2,\mathcal{L})$ which is covered by Hecke curves.
item.dc:creator: Lingguang Li, Hongyi Zhang

item.title: Tropical Degrees and Stable Intersections
item.description: arXiv:2605.24966v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study finite set-theoretic intersections of tropical curves with tropical hypersurfaces. An elementary divisor argument bounds their cardinality by the weighted sum of the Newton support function over the unbounded directions of the curve, without a transversality hypothesis. For tropical lines the bound is $h_\Delta(1,\dots,1)+\sum_i h_\Delta(-e_i)=n!\,\MV(\Delta,\Sigma,\dots,\Sigma)$. Explicit examples show that neither the $\ell^1$-diameter nor the support cardinality minus one gives a corresponding bound for tropical lines. We also record width refinements of the classical-line estimate of Lang, Shapiro and Shustin. A self-contained account of the standard transverse multiplicity formulas explains the role of saturated normal lattices and mixed-cell volumes. Finally, applying the tropical Bernstein theorem to locally independent subsystems gives a mixed-volume bound for the regular transverse locus of a redundant system. An example shows why a fixed subsystem need not compute the count on the whole redundant intersection.
item.dc:creator: Mounir Nisse

item.title: Transversal unfoldings of derived foliations
item.description: arXiv:2606.04253v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study when a derived foliation along the fibres of a smooth morphism extends transversally to the total space. We classify strict unfoldings by basic Lie derivations, retaining the automorphisms arising from central isotropy. We define an intrinsic space of unfoldings and prove its agreement with the strict classification when the relative cotangent complex is a vector bundle in degree zero. A counterexample shows that the strict construction is not invariant under equivalent presentations. For two-term cotangent complexes, we describe cotangent extensions and their integrability conditions, and obtain cohomological existence criteria for strict unfoldings in explicit families. On smooth representable leaf spaces, descended unfoldings correspond to integrable Ehresmann connections.
item.dc:creator: Maur\'icio Corr\^ea

item.title: On the Chow ring of very general abelian varieties and a question of Pirola
item.description: arXiv:2607.07053v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that for a very general abelian variety of dimension $\geq 4$, a divisor $D\in {\rm CH}^1(A)$ that satisfies $D^2=0$ in ${\rm CH}^2(A)$ is of torsion. The same result is also established for a very general Jacobian in genus $4$. We use then the second statement in order to prove a conjecture of Pirola, which states that any rational section of the Kummer fibration $K=J/\pm {\rm Id}\rightarrow \mathcal{M}_4$, where $J\rightarrow \mathcal{M}_4 $ is the Jacobian fibration, must be a multiple of the Griffiths-Pirola section given by the difference of the two trigonal divisors.
item.dc:creator: Claire Voisin

item.title: Composition of Sarkisov links between del Pezzo surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2607.13270v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that for any two birationally equivalent del Pezzo surfaces of Picard rank one over a perfect field there is a birational map between them such that it is decomposed in a composition of at most two Sarkisov links.
item.dc:creator: Anastasia V. Vikulova

item.title: The arithmetic de Rham stack
item.description: arXiv:2608.20203v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define and study the arithmetic de Rham stack $X^{\operatorname{arith}}$ of a scheme $X$ over a field of characteristic $p$, and analyze its relation with related stacks such as the Hyodo--Kato stack. We show that $X^{\operatorname{arith}}$ gives a stack-theoretic approach to rigid cohomology and its coefficients, known as overconvergent isocrystals and arithmetic $D$-modules, which avoids the long-standing problem of frame-choosing in earlier approaches. We finally give some arithmetic applications of our formalism, such as a proof of Berthelot's conjecture on the preservation of overconvergent isocrystals by smooth proper pushforward.
item.dc:creator: Junhui Qin

item.title: On smooth affine surfaces with the cohomology of a smooth curve
item.description: arXiv:2608.23021v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that if a smooth affine complex surface has the same integral mixed Hodge structure as a smooth curve whose compactification is of positive genus, then it admits a smooth morphism to the curve with fibers isomorphic to $\mathbb{A}^1$. In particular, every such surface is the total space of a torsor for a line bundle on the curve. The motivation comes from Jouanolou's trick, to which this result gives a kind of converse in dimension $2$. We also give an example in the case of $\mathbb{P}^1$ which has the same integral mixed Hodge structure as $\mathbb{P}^1$ and simply connected but does not admit a smooth $\mathbb{A}^1$ fibration over $\mathbb{P}^1$.
item.dc:creator: Arnab Roy

item.title: Representation Varieties of Stacks and Trace Maps
item.description: arXiv:2609.09633v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define a derived stack $\mathscr{Rep}_n(X)$ which generalizes the assignment $A\leadsto \operatorname{Rep}_n(A)$ to an algebra of its derived $GL_n$-representation variety of arXiv:1112.1449 from algebras $A$ to perfect stacks $X$ over characteristic 0 fields. In the case of a quasi-projective classical scheme $X$, we show that $\mathscr{Rep}_n(X)$ admits a subfunctor $\operatorname{Quot}^{n,\text{fr}}_{\mathscr{O}_X^n}(X)\subset \mathscr{Rep}_n(X)$, which is in fact represented by a derived scheme almost of finite type. We further construct a Fourier-Mukai integral transform between the derived categories of quasi-coherent sheaves on $X$ and $\operatorname{Quot}^{n,\text{fr}}_{\mathscr{O}_X^n}(X)$ which induces a trace map at the level of Hochschild homology generalizing the trace morphism constructed in arXiv:1112.1449 (for finitely presented commutative algebras). We show that the subfunctor $\operatorname{Quot}^{n,\text{fr}}_{\mathscr{O}_X^n}(X)$ is a derived enhancement of the framed locus of the Quot scheme of points and that this derived scheme is a $GL_n$-torsor over the stack of coherent length $n$ torsion sheaves. Hence, this stack is an analog of the derived character stack for quasi-projective schemes, and we show that for smooth, Calabi-Yau $X$, it inherits a shifted symplectic structure in the sense of arXiv:1111.3209 from the one constructed in arXiv:1812.11913 on the moduli stack of perfect complexes with proper support. This structure is shown to give a generalization of the classical symplectic structure on character varieties of surfaces of genus 1 constructed by Goldman \cite{gold}.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Erlikhman

item.title: On the quadratic length of plane Cremona maps of degree 4
item.description: arXiv:2609.39943v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Every non-linear plane Cremona map can be decomposed into quadratic maps, and the minimum number of quadratic maps required is called its quadratic length. It is known that plane Cremona maps of degree 3 have quadratic length either 2 or 3. In this paper, we study the quadratic length of plane Cremona maps $\varphi$ of degree 4. Recall that either $\varphi$ is de Jonqui\`eres, i.e. it has a base point of multiplicity 3, or it is not de Jonqui\`eres. In the latter case, $\varphi$ has quadratic length 2, whereas in the former case we prove that $\varphi$ has quadratic length 3, 4, or 5, and we classify those maps that reach the upper bound.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Calabri, Nguyen Thi Ngoc Giao

item.title: On wall-crossing invariant combinations of Welschinger numbers for rational surfaces with a conic bundle
item.description: arXiv:2610.02445v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We refine the real enumerative invariants insensitive to changes in the real structure introduced in our previous paper on del Pezzo surfaces, and extend these refined invariants to arbitrary rational surfaces. The construction involves a choice of an auxiliary conic bundle together with a Pin-structure. We prove that the resulting invariants are independent of these auxiliary choices and establish recursive relations for their computation.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Finashin, Viatcheslav Kharlamov

item.title: Smoothness criterion for Fano orbifolds and bases of Lagrangian fibrations
item.description: arXiv:2610.20496v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a smoothness criterion for Fano varieties with quotient singularities. As an application, we show that if $X\to B$ is a Lagrangian fibration from a compact hyper-K\"ahler manifold and $B$ has quotient singularities, then $B$ is a projective space.
item.dc:creator: Zhiyu Liu

item.title: Codimension of Brill-Noether Loci on Abelian Surfaces and the First Segre Invariant
item.description: arXiv:2610.24251v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be an abelian surface of Picard rank 1 with ample generator $H$. We show that, for a Mukai vector $\mathbf{v}=(r,mH,\chi)$ with $r,m\geq 1$ and $\chi\leq 0$, the first Brill-Noether loci $\{E \;|\; H^0(E)\neq 0\}$ in $M_X(\mathbf{v})$ is nonempty of the expected codimension $1-\chi$. As an application, we study the rank 1 Segre invariant on these abelian surfaces. Specifically, for $\mathbf{v}$ a Mukai vector of a $\mu$-stable sheaf of $\mathrm{rank}\geq 2$, we compute the Segre invariant of the general sheaf in $M_X(\mathbf{v})$, and we determine the numbers which arise as the Segre invariant of a sheaf in $M_X(\mathbf{v})$.
item.dc:creator: Jesse Chien

item.title: Canonical Projectivization of Algebraic Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.04314v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct canonical projective birational models of normal proper integral algebraic spaces over arbitrary fields. The construction preserves the intrinsic quasi-projective core and is natural under semilinear isomorphisms. For smooth proper integral input in characteristic zero, we combine an intrinsic choice of ideals with W{\l}odarczyk's principalization to obtain a canonical tower of blowups in smooth centers ending in a smooth projective variety. Consequently, every compact connected Moishezon manifold admits a smooth projective bimeromorphic model to which all automorphisms lift compatibly. The main ingredient is a family-sum argument yielding an intrinsic finite selection of maximal tuples of boundary ideal germs; successive modifications strictly decrease the boundary-image dimension. We also construct canonical quasi-projective models for nonproper normal input and a greatest schematizing ideal for separated finite-type algebraic spaces over noetherian bases. Oda's threefold illustrates the construction.
item.dc:creator: Parsa Bakhtary

item.title: On some formality criteria for DG-Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:1310.3048v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give some formality criteria for a differential graded Lie algebra to be formal. For instance, we show that a DG-Lie algebra L is formal if and only if the natural spectral sequence computing the Chevalley-Eilenberg cohomology H(L,L) degenerates at second page.
item.dc:creator: Marco Manetti

item.title: $(G,\mu)$-Windows and Deformations of $(G,\mu)$-Displays
item.description: arXiv:2011.09163v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $k_0$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$, let $G$ be a smooth affine group scheme over $\mathbb{Z}_p$, and let $\mu$ be a cocharacter of $G_{W(k_0)}$ such that the set of $\mu$-weights of $\Lie G$ is a subset of $\{-1,0,1,2,\dots\}$. We prove that the groupoid of adjoint nilpotent $(G,\mu)$-displays as in \cite[Definition 1.0.1]{pappas}, \cite{lau2} and \cite[Definition 3.16]{E7} is equivalent to the groupoid of $(G,\mu)$-windows, which are the generalizations of windows as in \cite[Definition 5.1]{langer2} and \cite[Definition 3.3.1]{E7}.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Bueltel, Mohammad Hadi Hedayatzadeh

item.title: Calligraphs and sphere realizations
item.description: arXiv:2308.15305v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a recursive procedure for computing the number of realizations of a minimally rigid graph on the sphere up to rotations. We accomplish this by combining two ingredients. The first is a framework that allows us to think of such realizations as of elements of a moduli space of stable rational curves with marked points. The second is the idea of splitting a minimally rigid graph into two subgraphs, called calligraphs, that admit one degree of freedom and that share only a single edge and a further vertex. This idea has been recently employed for realizations of graphs in the plane up to isometries. The key result is that we can associate to a calligraph a triple of natural numbers with a special property: whenever a minimally rigid graph is split into two calligraphs, the number of realizations of the former equals the product of the two triples of the latter, where this product is specified by a fixed quadratic form. These triples and quadratic form codify the fact that we express realizations as intersections of two curves on the blowup of a sphere along two pairs of complex conjugate points.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Gallet, Georg Grasegger, Niels Lubbes, Josef Schicho

item.title: On the Drinfeld formal group
item.description: arXiv:2403.02555v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We identify Drinfeld's formal group on the prismatization of $\mathrm{Spf}\,\mathbb{Z}_p$ with a formal group arising from homotopy theory, given locally by the Quillen formal group of a decompleted variant of topological periodic cyclic homology. We also prove that this formal group extends to the syntomization of $\mathrm{Spf}\,\mathbb{Z}_p$, and that it admits a certain algebraization conjectured by Drinfeld.
item.dc:creator: Deven Manam

item.title: Orbit structures and complexity in Schubert and Richardson Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2405.13774v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The goal of this paper is twofold. Firstly, we provide a type-uniform formula for the torus complexity of the usual torus action on a Richardson variety, by developing the notion of algebraic dimensions of Bruhat intervals, strengthening a type $A$ result by Donten-Bury, Escobar and Portakal. In the process, we give an explicit description of the torus action on any Deodhar component as well as describe the root subgroups that comprise the component. Secondly, when a Levi subgroup in a reductive algebraic group acts on a Schubert variety, we exhibit a codimension preserving bijection between the Levi-Borel subgroup (a Borel subgroup in the Levi subgroup) orbits in the big open cell of that Schubert variety and torus orbits in the big open cell of a distinguished Schubert subvariety. This bijection has many applications including a type-uniform formula for the Levi-Borel complexity of the usual Levi-Borel subgroup action on a Schubert variety. We conclude by extending the Levi-Borel complexity results to a large class of Schubert varieties in the partial flag variety.
item.dc:creator: Yibo Gao, Reuven Hodges

item.title: The Bruce-Roberts number of holomorphic 1-forms along complex analytic varieties
item.description: arXiv:2409.01237v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce the notion of the \textit{Bruce--Roberts number} for holomorphic 1-forms relative to complex analytic varieties. Our main result shows that the Bruce--Roberts number of a 1-form $\omega$ relative to a complex analytic hypersurface $X$ with an isolated singularity can be expressed in terms of the \textit{Gom\'ez-Mont--Seade--Verjovsky index} of $\omega$ along $X$, the \textit{Milnor number} of $\omega$ and the \textit{Tjurina number} of $X$. This result allows us to recover known formulas for the Bruce--Roberts number of a holomorphic function along $X$ and to establish connections between this number, the radial index, and the local Euler obstruction of $\omega$ along $X$. Moreover, we present applications to both global and local holomorphic foliations in complex dimension two.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Barbosa, Arturo Fern\'andez-P\'erez, V\'ictor Le\'on

item.title: Torsion of elliptic curves over quartic number fields with rational $j$-invariant
item.description: arXiv:2501.00400v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve defined over a quartic extension $K$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ with $j(E)\in\mathbb{Q}$. We classify the possible group structures of $E(K)_{\mathrm{tors}}$, concluding that the only additional possibilities, besides those occuring over quartic fields by base change from elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$, are $\mathbb{Z}/17\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/21\mathbb{Z}$.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Hamada

item.title: Cohomological Mackey formula for quotient stacks
item.description: arXiv:2505.09483v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we construct a restriction morphism on the critical cohomology of an equivariant Landau-Ginzburg model associated to a representation of a reductive group equipped with an invariant function. We show a compatibility formula between this restriction map and the induction map considered in earlier work in the form of a Mackey-type formula, thereby giving the critical cohomology the structure of a localized induction-restriction system. In the case of quivers, our formulas give the localized coproduct of Davison for cohomological Hall algebras of quivers with potential.
item.dc:creator: Lucien Hennecart

item.title: Bounded ratios for Lorentzian matrices
item.description: arXiv:2510.25030v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study multiplicative inequalities among entries of Lorentzian matrices, referred to as bounded ratios. These inequalities can be viewed as generalizations of the classical Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for mixed volumes. Our main structural result identifies the cone of all bounded ratios on Lorentzian matrices with the dual of the cut cone, a finitely generated integral polyhedral cone extensively studied in metric geometry and graph theory. We examine in detail the pentagonal ratio, which first appears for Lorentzian matrices of size at least five. For Lorentzian matrices of size three, we determine the optimal bounding constants across the entire cone of bounded ratios, obtaining an explicit entropy-like formula.
item.dc:creator: Daoji Huang, June Huh, Daniel Soskin, Botong Wang

item.title: Cellular free resolutions for normalizations of toric ideals
