item.description: arXiv:2512.17871v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For any toric ideal $I$ in a polynomial ring $S$, we provide a combinatorial description of a free resolution of the integral closure of the $S$-module $S/I$. These new complexes arise from an extension of Bayer--Sturmfels' theory of cellular free resolutions. As applications, we unify several constructions for a resolution of the diagonal embedding of a toric variety, and compare the locally free resolutions for toric subvarieties introduced by Hanlon--Hicks--Lazarev and Brown--Erman.
item.dc:creator: Christine Berkesch, Lauren Cranton Heller, Gregory G. Smith, Jay Yang

item.title: Some examples of DG-Lie formality transfer
item.description: arXiv:2601.19698v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a convenient reformulation, a slight generalization and some applications of the formality transfer theorem for DG-Lie algebras.
item.dc:creator: Marco Manetti, Gabriele Rossetti

item.title: A uniform decomposition theorem for invariant differential operators on imprimitive complex reflection groups G(r,p,n)
item.description: arXiv:2608.01474v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: {We study the module structure of the polynomial ring, localized at the discriminant, over the ring of differential operators on the ring of invariants of the imprimitive complex reflection group $G(r,p,n)$, describing its simple components with explicit generators given by the higher Specht polynomials of Ariki--Terasoma--Yamada. The proof rests on a Jacobian lemma computing the discriminant of $G(r,p,n)$, combined with a double-centralizer argument. As particular cases ($r=2$, $p=2$ or $p=1$) we recover, and considerably shorten, the known decomposition theorems for the real reflection groups $W(D_n)$ and $W(B_n)$; we also treat $G(r,r,n)$ and $G(r,1,n)$ explicitly, with worked examples ($D_2$, $D_3$, $B_2$) and their central idempotents. Finally, applying the Galois descent equivalence of categories of Nonkan\'e to $G(r,p,n)$ for the first time gives a second, generator-free description of the simple summands as twisted invariants.}
item.dc:creator: Jean Kabor\'e, Ibrahim Nonkan\'e

item.title: Critical-point-free energy for fractional-Toledo representations
item.description: arXiv:2608.15714v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $S_g$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g\ge2$. For a reductive representation $\rho:\pi_1(S_g)\to\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$, let $E_\rho$ be the energy function on Teichm\"uller space associated to equivariant harmonic maps into $\mathrm{CH}^2$. For every positive integer $d$ with $3\nmid d$, all sufficiently large $h$, and every $g>h$, we construct an irreducible reductive representation \[ \rho_{g,h,d}:\pi_1(S_g)\to\mathrm{PU}(2,1) \] with \[ \tau(\rho_{g,h,d})=2h-2-\frac{2d}{3}\notin\mathbb Z, \qquad \mathrm{Crit}(E_{\rho_{g,h,d}})=\varnothing. \] Consequently, the associated branched-minimal-surface forgetful map is not surjective in these nonintegral Toledo components.
item.dc:creator: Rivu Bardhan, Anu Dhochak, Pradip Kumar

item.title: Rational homotopy theory of flag manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2609.30591v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $G/P$ be a flag manifold with $G$ simple. We determine the rational homotopy groups $\pi _{\ast }(G/P)\otimes \mathbb{Q}$ and describe the rational cohomology ring $H^{\ast }(G/P;\mathbb{Q})$ solely in terms of the rational homotopy types of $G$ and $P$, respectively. The proof is based on the restrictions of basic Weyl invariants of $G$ to suitable simple factors of $P$, which also address a key nonvanishing issue not settled by earlier approaches of Meier, Shiga-Tezuka, Kotschick, and Terzic.
item.dc:creator: Haibao Duan

item.title: Profinite Non-Rigidity of Arithmetic Lattices and the K\"ahler Property
item.description: arXiv:2609.31523v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the K\"ahlerness of a finitely presented, residually finite group is not determined by its profinite completion, which answers a question asked independently by Arapura and Libgober. In the proof, we give explicit constructions to characterize the absolute Dynkin types that admit non-isomorphic real forms of higher-rank Lie groups containing torsion-free arithmetic lattices with isomorphic profinite completions.
item.dc:creator: Yukun Du, Feng Hao, Kejia Zhu

item.title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.29211v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that for every open $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory $\theta(t)$, $t \geq 0$, of a definable $C^1$-potential $F \colon U \to \mathbb{R}$ has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable $C^1$-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field. Notably, the gradient trajectory in this result is an arbitrary solution of the gradient flow differential equation (whose solutions may not be unique) with no further assumptions: The gradient trajectory may be unbounded and diverge to infinity or it may be convergent. The established theorem therefore provides affirmative answers to both the gradient conjecture at infinity for definable potentials and the definable Thom gradient conjecture. We extend our conclusions from the Euclidean metric to a general class of ambient metrics including Riemannian metrics and we establish uniform local upper bounds for the lengths of the spherical projections of gradient flow trajectories. We finally apply our findings to the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) to conclude that, in the case of definable and continuously differentiable activation and loss functions, the spherical projection of the DNN training flow must always converge (directional convergence).
item.dc:creator: Thang Do, Arnulf Jentzen, Benno Kuckuck

item.title: Intersection multiplicity of a sparse curve and a trinomial curve
item.description: arXiv:2610.35037v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let f $\in$ C[x, y] be a trinomial and let g $\in$ C[x, y] be a sparse polynomial with N monomials (N $\ge$ 1). We address the problem of bounding the local intersection multiplicity of the bivariate polynomial system f = g = 0 at an isolated root q $\in$ (C * )^ 2 only in terms of N . Our main result establishes that the local multiplicity of the system at any isolated solution q $\in$ (C * ) ^2 is at most (N -1)(N +2)/ 2 , independently of the degrees of f and g. Furthermore, we know that this bound is sharp for N = 3.
item.dc:creator: Jean Mousseau (LAMA)

item.title: Common zeros of homogeneous polynomials and the weight hierarchy of projective Reed-Muller codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.08203v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the maximum number of common zeros in projective space of any set of linearly independent homogeneous polynomials of the same degree, when the degree is smaller than the cardinality of the finite field. This proves the conjecture of Beelen, Datta, and Ghorpade, resolving a longstanding problem on common zeros and determining the complete weight hierarchy of the corresponding projective Reed-Muller codes. The proof uses Green's hyperplane restriction bound, combined with a footprint argument that reduces the problem to the affine case solved by Heijnen and Pellikaan. Wei duality then determines the hierarchy in sufficiently large degrees, recovering the complete hierarchy in every degree for the projective plane. Finally, we prove an upper bound valid in every degree, and conjecture that it is always sharp.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo San-Jos\'e
